case_title: SRI RAMESHWAR YADA V & ORS. v. THE STATE OF BIHAR & ANR.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498A, s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act
evidence_type: Written application, distance and residence details
neutral_facts: The second respondent filed a complaint against the accused-appellants and the husband of the complainant, alleging offences under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The magistrate summoned the accused and the husband for the case. The accused filed an application seeking exemption from personal appearance in the trial, citing their residence in Pune and the long distance to the trial location in Patna. The magistrate rejected the application, citing reasons such as the accused appearing healthy and the need for conciliation. The accused appealed to the High Court, which dismissed the application on the grounds that the application under Section 205 Cr.P.C. was filed after the accused had already appeared in court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, finding that the High Court's reasoning was unfounded and that the magistrate should have considered the grounds for exemption provided by the accused.
